title: Exforge (amlodipine/valsartan): EPAR product information, Annex I summary of product characteristics
authors: European Medicines Agency (marketing authorisation holder Novartis Europharm Limited)
journal: European Medicines Agency, European public assessment report, product information; PDF created 16 September 2025, modified 12 November 2025
funder: not stated; EU product information carries no funding statement
result: Contraindications include hypersensitivity to dihydropyridine derivatives, severe hypotension, shock including cardiogenic shock, obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract (for example hypertrophic obstructive cardiomyopathy and high-grade aortic stenosis) and haemodynamically unstable heart failure after acute myocardial infarction. Warnings: safety and efficacy of amlodipine in hypertensive crisis are not established; in PRAISE-2 amlodipine in NYHA III and IV heart failure of non-ischaemic aetiology was associated with increased reports of pulmonary oedema despite no significant difference in worsening heart failure; calcium channel blockers, including amlodipine, should be used with caution in congestive heart failure, as they may increase the risk of future cardiovascular events and mortality; special caution with mitral stenosis or significant aortic stenosis that is not high grade. Interactions linked to amlodipine: grapefruit or grapefruit juice is not recommended because bioavailability may increase in some patients; strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (protease inhibitors, azole antifungals, erythromycin, clarithromycin, verapamil, diltiazem) may significantly increase exposure, with clinical effects possibly more pronounced in the elderly; CYP3A4 inducers (carbamazepine, phenobarbital, phenytoin, fosphenytoin, primidone, rifampicin, Hypericum perforatum) may alter plasma concentration; simvastatin limited to 20 mg daily (77% exposure increase at 80 mg); risk of increased tacrolimus levels; in animals lethal ventricular fibrillation and cardiovascular collapse with hyperkalaemia followed verapamil and intravenous dantrolene, so co-administration of calcium channel blockers such as amlodipine is to be avoided in people susceptible to malignant hyperthermia and in its management. Pregnancy: safety not established; use only when no safer alternative exists. Breastfeeding: infant dose interquartile range 3 to 7% of the maternal dose, maximum 15%. Fertility: reversible biochemical changes in the head of spermatozoa reported in some patients treated with calcium channel blockers; in one rat study a dose comparable to the human dose for 30 days lowered follicle-stimulating hormone, testosterone, sperm density and mature spermatid and Sertoli cell numbers. Amlodipine adverse reactions by frequency: common somnolence, dizziness, headache, palpitations, flushing, abdominal pain, nausea, ankle swelling, oedema, fatigue; uncommon depression, mood changes, insomnia, syncope, hypotension, change of bowel habit, micturition disorder, impotence, gynaecomastia; rare confusion; very rare leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hyperglycaemia, peripheral neuropathy, myocardial infarction, arrhythmia (including bradycardia, ventricular tachycardia and atrial fibrillation), vasculitis, pancreatitis, gastritis, gingival hyperplasia, hepatitis, intrahepatic cholestasis and jaundice, hepatic enzyme increase mostly consistent with cholestasis, angioedema, erythema multiforme, exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome, Quincke oedema; not known toxic epidermal necrolysis and extrapyramidal syndrome. Peripheral oedema in double-blind trials: amlodipine 10 mg alone 10.3%, with valsartan 160 mg 9.0% and 320 mg 9.5%; amlodipine 2.5 mg alone 8.0%; placebo 3.0%. Overdose: marked and potentially prolonged systemic hypotension including shock with fatal outcome has been reported; non-cardiogenic pulmonary oedema has rarely been reported after amlodipine overdose, may appear 24 to 48 hours after ingestion and require ventilatory support, and early resuscitative measures including fluid overload may be precipitating factors. Pharmacology: amlodipine does not change sinoatrial nodal function or atrioventricular conduction in intact animals or humans; bioavailability 64 to 80%, about 97.5% protein bound, terminal half-life 30 to 50 hours. ALLHAT (33,357 patients, mean 4.9 years): heart failure 10.2% with amlodipine against 7.7% with chlorthalidone (RR 1.38, 95% CI 1.25 to 1.52); all-cause mortality RR 0.96 (0.89 to 1.02).
